items.name: Page verdict vocabulary (`genai_evidence` 4 values vs v2.7 8-value page verdict)
items.current_text:
v2.5 (production) §4.7:

- `confirms_activity` | Source documents a specific GenAI activity at this institution
- `confirms_absence` | The supplied page text contains no GenAI evidence relevant to this institution
- `ambiguous` | Source mentions AI but unclear whether generative AI, or mentions GenAI but unclear whether this institution is involved
- `background_only` | Source provides general context (country AI strategy, vendor overview) but does not document activity at this specific institution

SPEC R-015 (locked): "Page-verdict vocabulary has 8 values: the 7 re-pilot 2 values (`confirms_activity`, `ambiguous_genai`, `ambiguous_attribution`, `other_body` = v2.6 `other_actor`, `event_only` = v2.6 `excluded_event`, `background_only`, `no_genai`) plus v2.5 `confirms_absence` (page states absence; distinct from `no_genai`, no relevant content). It replaces v2.5 `genai_evidence` in the same column."

Re-pilot 2 jev instruction (unclear2.py L84-85): "Code this PAGE for the named institution only, using only what the page says. Does it document a generative-AI activity at this institution? If several values fit, take the first in this order." Definitions at unclear2.py L33-54 (confirms_activity text quoted under C02/C04; `event_only`: "The only GenAI content is a public-facing event, workshop, seminar, showcase or educational programme, with no documented adoption, procurement, deployment or governance by the institution itself (WS10 D1: not a qualifying activity)."; `background_only`: "The page gives only general context (national AI strategy, vendor overview, news about GenAI in general) and documents no activity at this institution."; `no_genai`: "The page contains no generative-AI content relevant to this institution.")

chosen.label: R-015 as locked: 8 values (re-pilot 2 wording + `confirms_absence` = page states absence)
chosen.mechanism: One jev Choice with 8 values and a first-in-order tie-break; v2.5 rows keep 4-value answers, told apart by row contract version.
chosen.benefits: Already ruled. 7 of the 8 values were piloted (re-pilot 2, $0.097). Separates the WS10 categories.
chosen.risks: The findings above: the same token means three things, `confirms_absence` is undefined and unpiloted, `ambiguous_attribution` is collapsing, and the chunk rule conflicts with R-044.
chosen.commits_to: An enum change: two contract-version steps (C-007), regenerated jev question set, contract-pin goldens, and the procurement copy of the enums (R-085 / D-008). A-011 fixtures for all 8 values, including a fixture for page-stated absence.

items.name: Generative-AI boundary (what counts as GenAI; chatbot / assistant rule)
items.current_text:
v2.5 system prompt L11: "**Include:** large language models (GPT, Claude, Gemini, LLaMA, Mistral, etc.), text-to-image generators, code-generation tools (GitHub Copilot, Amazon CodeWhisperer), sovereign/national LLMs (France's Albert, etc.), GenAI-powered chatbots, and any tool explicitly described as using generative AI, LLMs, or foundation models." L13: "**Exclude:** traditional machine learning (fraud detection classifiers, predictive analytics), robotic process automation (RPA) without a generative component, rule-based chatbots without LLM backends, general "AI strategies" that do not specifically reference generative AI." L15-21: positive signal required (1 named LLM/product, 2 explicit generative-capability description incl. "drafts, writes, summarizes, translates, or generates", 3 explicit label); "A "chatbot," "virtual assistant," or "automation" mentioned **without** one of these three signals is not sufficient evidence of GenAI activity".

Re-pilot 2 (unclear2.py L36, L41-44): "The text must be explicitly generative AI (LLMs, ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, AI chatbots, AI-generated content or equivalents) ... Generic 'AI', 'artificial intelligence', 'smart' systems, automation, analytics, prediction, transcription, translation, image or video recognition, or traditional machine-learning tools do not count unless the page says the tool generates text, images, audio, code or other content, or names a generative product or model (e.g. ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, Claude, an LLM, an AI chatbot or AI assistant)."

SPEC R-016: "A named "AI chatbot" or "AI assistant" counts as generative and overrides the rule-based-chatbot exclusion (contract L12) for that naming. Contract §4.1 is unchanged: a generic "AI strategy" or "AI tools" stays `unclear`".

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: R-016 boundary plus a stored mechanism basis
chosen.mechanism: Keep R-016, and record for every positive which signal established GenAI (A01: named product/model, explicit label, generative capability described, named AI chatbot/assistant only). Also settle translation: (a) "translation counts only when the page ties it to a named GenAI product or says it is generated by an LLM", or (b) "translation counts as generative capability". The PI picks a or b.
chosen.benefits: Keeps the ruled boundary while letting analysts drop R-016-only positives in a robustness check. Resolves the translation contradiction explicitly.
chosen.risks: One more jev question per positive page. The PI still has to choose a or b on translation.
chosen.commits_to: Adding A01 (a new field: schema, API and site columns). A small re-pilot of the A01 question.

items.name: Institution-level `has_genai_activity` and the rule that a page cannot issue institution-wide `no`
items.current_text:
v2.5 §4.1: "`yes` | At least one source documents a specific GenAI tool, pilot, policy, or deployment at this institution. `no` | All supplied pages for this institution have been reviewed and contain no mention of GenAI, LLMs, ChatGPT, Copilot, or equivalents. `unclear` | Ambiguous signals that could indicate GenAI activity but cannot be confirmed."

v2.6 system prompt (Per-page verdict): "A single supplied page cannot establish completion of the institution's remaining evidence review. Emit has_genai_activity=yes when this page supports a qualifying activity at the searched institution; otherwise emit unclear, including a clearly excluded event or no-qualifying-content page. Stage 6 determines a reviewed-evidence no only after the pipeline supplies complete context and no unresolved signal."

SPEC R-005: "institution-level `no` only with complete supplied context and no unresolved signal. An institution whose reviewed pages are all negative at confidence ≥ 0.8 gets `no` directly; the complete-context rule blocks `no` only when an unresolved signal remains (a low-confidence negative downgraded under R-081 counts as one)."

chosen.label: v2.6 + R-005: pages emit yes/unclear only; Stage 6 `no` when all pages negative at ≥0.8 and no unresolved signal
chosen.mechanism: Deterministic Stage 6 rule over the page verdicts and confidences.
chosen.benefits: Already ruled. Prevents page-level `no`. Simple to implement.
chosen.risks: The negative set and the failed-page treatment are undefined. The `no` label overstates. The v2.5 §4.1 text still contradicts it.
chosen.commits_to: Writing the negative-set table and the failed-page rule into the codebook (a PI line-edit). No enum change.

items.name: Attribution and other-body rules
items.current_text:
v2.5 system prompt L29: "Check that the page actually pertains to the named institution and not a similarly-named entity (different country, different level of government, parent ministry rather than this agency, etc.). If the page describes a different entity, code `genai_evidence = confirms_absence`". L32 (step 4): GenAI not tied to this institution -> `ambiguous`. L33 (step 5): country-wide program without naming the institution -> `ambiguous` + `institution_attribution`. L52: "Attribute activities to the specific institution in the batch, not to its parent ministry or country. If a national initiative exists but this institution's participation is unconfirmed, use `unclear` with flag `institution_attribution`."

Re-pilot 2 confirms_activity (L37-41): "The activity must be carried out or adopted by the named institution itself. Exclude activity by a parent, higher-level or neighbouring body (e.g. a district, county, regency, region, consortium or city department when the named institution is a village, ward or sub-unit), by a similarly named organisation or company, and pages by vendors that only use the place name." `other_body` (L47-51): "The page documents a generative-AI activity, but it clearly belongs to a different body, not the named institution ...". `ambiguous_attribution` (L46).

v2.6 L39-46: observed actor separate from query target; "External speakers, service providers, courts, similarly named counties and joint projects do not inherit that identity."

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: add a two-direction grain rule and observed-actor extraction
chosen.mechanism: Add to confirms_activity: "An activity carried out by an organisational unit of the named institution (department, office, service) counts for the named institution. An activity of its parent, a sibling, or a separate court, board or authority does not, unless the page says the named institution takes part." Add a joint rule: "A joint activity counts when the page names this institution as a participant." Extract `observed_actor` (A05) on every confirms_activity, other_body and ambiguous_attribution page.
chosen.benefits: Settles the downward direction. Keeps other-body evidence usable for later correction-layer transfers.
chosen.risks: "Separate court, board or authority" needs a list per country (the Butler-type case). A county's activity is not credited to its parent state, which may be the wrong call for some analyses. Adds extractor output.
chosen.commits_to: Re-pilot of the amended confirms_activity text. A05 schema addition. Fixtures for unit, parent and joint cases.

items.name: WS10 action boundary (events, governance, staff training, proposals)
items.current_text:
v2.6 system prompt L27-37: "Record institution-specific GenAI adoption, procurement, deployment, governance, and explicitly GenAI institution-specific proposals. Public workshops, talks and educational events are excluded even when the institution hosts, funds or attends. An event source can independently document a qualifying action: evaluate that separate action, not the venue. Institution-directed staff GenAI training qualifies; training does not establish tool deployment. Formal institution-issued rules for internal personnel OR external users qualify, including prohibitions, submission rules, and approved-tool/privacy conditions. Record the issuing body's governance action separately from software use. A draft or agenda can support proposed activity without proving enactment. Proposed activity has no new commitment bar. Preserve proposed, announced, pilot, production and discontinued distinctions."

SPEC R-010..R-013 (WS10 D1-D4). D1 approved wording: "A public-facing GenAI event or educational program is not itself a qualifying activity. An event page can support a separate record when it explicitly documents the institution's own adoption, procurement, deployment, or governance. A demonstration alone does not establish deployment."

chosen.label: R-010..R-013 / v2.6 L27-37 as approved
chosen.mechanism: Boundary applied inside the verdict question (event_only) and in pass 2.
chosen.benefits: Signed (D1-D4). Piloted as `event_only`.
chosen.risks: "Formal" and "institution-directed" undefined. Incidental clauses count fully. DECYP fixture stale.
chosen.commits_to: Relabelling the DECYP fixture (PI sign). No enum change.

items.name: Group D gating (`_NA_` rule) and pass-2 scope
items.current_text:
v2.5 §3.2: "When `has_genai_activity` = `no` or `unclear`, OR the row's source is `confirms_absence` / `ambiguous` / `background_only`, set **every field in Group D** to the exact string `_NA_`." §6 check 2: "On every row where `genai_evidence` = `confirms_activity`, NO Group D column may be `_NA_` (use `unknown`, `none_reported`, `none`, or `not_documented` as appropriate instead)."

SPEC R-003: "The second pass runs on every page with GenAI content: `confirms_activity`, `ambiguous_genai`, `ambiguous_attribution`, `other_body`, `event_only`." R-015: "Rules that read the column (yes needs a `confirms_activity` row; activity fields `_NA_` otherwise) are updated to the 8 values."

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: add `not_applicable` and an applicability table by action type
chosen.mechanism: Add `not_applicable` to tool_name, vendor, deployment_mode, target_users, access_type and interaction_type. A published table states which fields apply to each action type (e.g. deployment_mode and access_type do not apply to governance, staff_training or proposal-without-tool). It is applied deterministically after jev, so jev is not asked inapplicable questions.
chosen.benefits: Separates "does not apply" from "unknown". Fewer jev questions for governance activities.
chosen.risks: Six enum changes. v2.5 `unknown` values on policy rows cannot be recoded without a rerun.
chosen.commits_to: An enum change: two contract-version steps (C-007), regenerated jev question set, contract-pin goldens, and the procurement copy of the enums (R-085 / D-008). Needs an action-type code (C08 alt-1 or A02).

items.name: Activity segmentation and `activity_name`
items.current_text:
v2.5 col 11: "`activity_name` | string | Max 120 chars / `_NA_` | Short name. Use official name if one exists (e.g., "MyCity Chatbot", "Pair Platform"). Otherwise descriptive (e.g., "Internal Copilot pilot for document drafting")." §4.2 rule: "If an institution has issued a GenAI policy AND is running a pilot, these are **two distinct activities**." §6 check 5: "For all rows sharing the same `activity_name`, the Group D columns (11-28) must be identical".

SPEC R-003: "After the first pass, the extraction model segments the page into one or more activities"; DEC-010 a: "nano returns character spans only; jev sees page with span marked".

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: a codebook definition of the activity unit, checked by jev
chosen.mechanism: Definition (draft): "One activity = one action (deployment, procurement, governance instrument, training, proposal) by one actor concerning one tool or instrument. Components of a named program are one activity, with the component noted. Repeated transactions for the same product by the same unit are one activity. A policy and the tools it approves are separate activities." The extractor proposes spans; jev answers per span: new distinct activity / same as span k / component of span k / not an activity.
chosen.benefits: jev makes the segmentation decision, so C-001 holds. Relations are recorded at page level, which feeds the R-005 Stage 6 relation rules.
chosen.risks: One more jev question per span. The definition is substantive and needs PI wording. Pass-1 cost rises on multi-activity pages.
chosen.commits_to: PI wording. Fixtures from the v2.6 relation cases. A pipeline change in the T-02x cards.

items.name: `activity_type`
items.current_text:
v2.5 §4.2: "`policy_guidance` | Executive orders, agency memos, acceptable-use rules, procurement standards, internal guidance on permissible GenAI tools and data handling. | `pilot_experiment` | Limited trials, sandboxes, proof-of-concept deployments, or time-bounded experiments. | `program_initiative` | Cross-agency programs, governance bodies, training programs, or platform rollouts spanning multiple units. | `internal_operational` | Routine internal use for drafting, summarization, knowledge search, translation, internal helpdesks, or developer tooling. | `public_facing_service` | Citizen- or business-facing chatbots, service navigation, translation, complaint handling, case triage. | `unknown` | Evidence confirms a GenAI activity at this institution, but the kind of undertaking is indeterminate ... never as a default."

v2.6 changes: policy_guidance adds "formal rules on permissible GenAI use for internal personnel and external users, including prohibitions and submission rules"; program_initiative "institution-directed staff GenAI training (not public events)"; internal_operational evidence "Documented tool use; approved-tool lists alone are governance, procurement alone is not production."

chosen.label: v2.5 values (v2.6 wording optional)
chosen.mechanism: One jev Choice, 6 values.
chosen.benefits: Comparable with every v2.5 activity row.
chosen.risks: Multi-dimensional, so reliability suffers. No procurement or training values.
chosen.commits_to: No change (or v2.6 wording only: no enum change).

items.name: `adoption_stage` (incl. §4.3 and the owed procurement amendment)
items.current_text:
v2.5 §4.3: "`proposed` | Exploratory or hedged intent with no concrete commitment: "considering," "exploring," "studying feasibility," early discussions, unfunded or undated ideas. The text must still be explicitly generative-AI and tied to this institution. No named tool tied to a timeline, no signed MoU or contract, no budget line, no adopted policy. | `announced` | Publicly stated intent to deploy with a concrete, documented commitment but no evidence of actual use. Includes: MoUs, budget allocations without deployment, strategy timelines. | `pilot` | Limited deployment: subset of users/departments/use cases; described as trial/pilot/PoC/experiment; time-bounded. | `production` | Fully operational: available to intended user base, no longer experimental, in routine operations. | `discontinued` | Previously deployed but explicitly ended, cancelled, or suspended. | `unknown` | Evidence confirms GenAI activity exists but stage is indeterminate." "Permanent pilot" rule: "If described as "pilot" but running >12 months AND serving the full intended user base, code `production`."

Owed: procurement subproject amendment to `proposed` (R-087), text NOT yet received; this review drafts alternatives that procurement must agree.

chosen.label: Agent-drafted (procurement must agree): separate `procurement_status` field
chosen.mechanism: Keep adoption_stage for use; add `procurement_status`: none_documented / tender_or_rfp / award_or_contract / payment_or_subscription / unknown. Payment-only activities get adoption_stage `unknown` (as in the Clay fixtures) plus procurement_status `payment_or_subscription`.
chosen.benefits: Two separate dimensions. The procurement pipeline can own the new field. No change to stage semantics.
chosen.risks: Two fields for related facts, and a new column on every activity.
chosen.commits_to: A new field (schema/API/site) plus enum steps for procurement. Coordination with the procurement integrator on ownership.

items.name: `access_type`
items.current_text: v2.5 §4.4: "`proprietary_vendor` | Commercial product (OpenAI, Microsoft, Google, Anthropic, etc.) via API or license. | `open_source` | Open-source model (LLaMA, Mistral, Falcon, etc.) self-hosted or via hosting provider. | `sovereign_model` | Model developed by/for a government with data-sovereignty goals (e.g., France's Albert, Germany's OpenGPT-X). | `in_house` | Built by the institution's own team, not based on a major external foundation model. | `mixed` | Combines types (e.g., proprietary API fine-tuned in-house, sovereign model on commercial cloud). | `unknown` | Cannot determine."

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: two fields, model origin and build arrangement
chosen.mechanism: `model_origin`: commercial / open_weight / government_developed / unknown. `build_arrangement`: off_the_shelf_product / custom_application_on_external_model / model_trained_or_fine_tuned_by_institution / unknown.
chosen.benefits: Each dimension stands alone and the commonest case has an obvious code.
chosen.risks: Two new fields replace one. The v2.5 series breaks (a crosswalk is only partial).
chosen.commits_to: An enum change: two contract-version steps (C-007), regenerated jev question set, contract-pin goldens, and the procurement copy of the enums (R-085 / D-008). New columns.

items.name: `interaction_type`
items.current_text: v2.5 §4.5: chatbot "Conversational interface for Q&A, navigation, or retrieval"; document_processing "Summarization, extraction, classification, or generation of documents" (examples "Drafting memos, summarizing reports, processing forms"); code_generation; decision_support "Analysis, recommendations, or scoring to aid human decisions" (examples "Case triage, fraud detection, eligibility assessment"); translation; content_creation "Generating public communications, social media, multimedia" (examples "Press releases, social media, report drafting"); search_retrieval "Semantic search, knowledge retrieval, RAG over internal stores"; multiple "Tool explicitly serves multiple interaction types by design"; not_applicable "For `policy_guidance` activities with no specific tool"; unknown.

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: split into interface plus function items
chosen.mechanism: `interface` (one Choice): conversational / embedded_in_existing_software / standalone_application / backend_or_api / not_applicable / unknown. Functions as separate jev yes/no items (jev returns one code per question): drafting_writing, summarization, translation, search_retrieval, code, image_audio_video, extraction_classification, analysis_recommendation. Each item is chunk-safe with any-yes.
chosen.benefits: Multi-label without `multiple`. Each item is binary and reliable. Fits jev's Choice-only design.
chosen.risks: About 9 jev questions per activity instead of 1. Breaks the series (crosswalk from single values to function items is lossy). Overlaps deployment_mode (C14).
chosen.commits_to: An enum change: two contract-version steps (C-007), regenerated jev question set, contract-pin goldens, and the procurement copy of the enums (R-085 / D-008). New columns (or a JSON list column), API/site changes. Re-pilot.

items.name: `vendor`
items.current_text:
v2.5 col 17: "`vendor` | string | Max 100 chars / `unknown` / `_NA_` | Vendor or provider. For in-house tools: the institution or its parent agency name."

v2.6 L56-57: "Do not infer a vendor from institutional authorship or insert unsupported product names into free text."

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: page-stated vendor plus a lookup with stated basis
chosen.mechanism: vendor = the organisation the page names as supplying the GenAI product or service, verbatim. If none is named but tool_name matches a published lookup table (product -> developer, versioned), fill it deterministically and set `vendor_basis` = lookup, otherwise `stated`.
chosen.benefits: Keeps coverage for well-known products, with transparent provenance.
chosen.risks: The lookup table needs upkeep and is a G3O artifact that can contain errors. Adds a column.
chosen.commits_to: A new column `vendor_basis` and a maintained table. Schema version step.

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: definitions + not_applicable
chosen.mechanism: "integrated: the GenAI feature works inside software or a service channel the institution already used (office suite, case system, existing website service). standalone: a separate application or site created for the GenAI tool." Add `not_applicable` for activities without a tool.

items.name: `year_announced`

v2.5 col 20: "`year_announced` | string | `YYYY` / `unknown` / `_NA_` | Year first publicly announced or documented."

DEC-009 a routing: "jev Choice: `year_announced`, `year_deployed`, CX-60/61; deterministic: contact emails, explicit years".

items.name: disclosure_form (CX-10..CX-18)
items.current_text:
Question to jev: *What kind of document is this page?* One value. If several fit, take the first in table order.

- `register_cross_institution`: The page is, or is one entry in, a structured list of AI or algorithmic systems kept by a government body, with several entries in a common format (inventory, register, catalogue, algorithmic transparency record in a standard template), **and the list covers more than one institution** (a national or sectoral register, a standard-template record series across agencies).
- `register_single_institution`: As CX-10, but the list covers **one institution only** (e.g. a city's own table of its AI tools).
- `mandated_report`: The page is a document produced to meet a reporting obligation, such as a statutory annual-report section or a compliance or transparency report under a named rule.
- CX-13: The obligation may be named on the page **or inferred from the document's genre** (e.g. an annual report, a statutory compliance report). This is the one stated exception to CX-03.
- `formal_record`: An official one-off document of record from a government body: adopted policy or guidance, legislation, council or board minutes or resolutions, budget documents, procurement notice or award, audit or inspection report, **response to a freedom-of-information request**.
- `informal_official`: A government body's own communication with no reporting obligation and no standard format: press release, news item, blog, social post, speech, event page, service or FAQ page.
- `third_party`: Not published by a government body: news, vendor, academic, NGO or policy organization. A register entry quoted in a news article is `third_party` (code the page, not what it quotes).
- `unknown`: The page's kind cannot be determined from its text (e.g. an archived fragment with no header).

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: require an AI-related obligation for mandated_report
chosen.mechanism: Re-word CX-12/13: `mandated_report` only when the obligation concerns reporting on AI, algorithms or digital systems, named on the page; genre inference allowed only for documents whose title names AI/algorithmic reporting. Otherwise statutory annual reports code `formal_record`.
chosen.benefits: Restores the 'systematic AI disclosure' construct; removes a CX-03 exception; gives the extractor a quotable anchor (the named rule).
chosen.risks: Lower `mandated_report` counts (already ~1%); re-opens D-B (b), a signed PI ruling.
chosen.commits_to: Re-signature of CX-12/13 (D-B); fixture pages for the new boundary (R-084); no enum change, so no version steps beyond the v2.7 already planned.

items.name: disclosure_scope (CX-20..CX-25)
items.current_text:
- `whole_of_government`: The listing or document the page belongs to covers institutions across the government (all central agencies, or all units of a level).
- `multi_institution`: It covers several institutions, but not government-wide (a sector, a region, a group of agencies).
- `single_institution`: It covers one institution only.
- `unknown`: Coverage cannot be determined from the page.
- CX-25: which pages are coded: All pages.

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: code scope only on register and mandated pages
chosen.mechanism: Ask `disclosure_scope` only when `disclosure_form` in {register_cross_institution, register_single_institution, mandated_report}; otherwise store `_NA_`.
chosen.benefits: Scope then measures the disclosure system as intended; fewer low-confidence answers; cheaper.
chosen.risks: Reverses D-D (b) (all pages); loses activity-scope information that some index variants might want.
chosen.commits_to: Re-signature of CX-25 (D-D); `_NA_` added to the value set (enum change, two version steps); CX-11's QC check unchanged.

items.name: evaluation_documented (CX-30..CX-40, incl. CX-32b/c/d, CX-33)
items.current_text:
Question to jev: *Does this page document an evaluation of this GenAI activity?* One value. If several fit, take the first in table order.

- `results_reported`: The page states that this activity was tested, evaluated, audited or monitored **and** reports a result (a metric, a finding or a conclusion).
- `conducted_no_results`: The page states that an evaluation, test, audit, pilot review or monitoring took place or is in place, but reports no result.
- `required_or_planned`: The page states that an evaluation is required (by a rule) or planned, with no evidence that it has happened. A policy finding that requires evaluation of GenAI tools takes this value.
- CX-32b: A requirement to carry out a risk or impact assessment is **not** `required_or_planned`; it belongs to `has_risk_assessment` alone (consistent with CX-37).
- CX-32c: A clause requiring periodic review of the GenAI policy itself counts as `required_or_planned`. This includes any policy with a GenAI section (e.g. a general IT policy).
- CX-32d: A required pre-use review that mixes fitness-for-purpose with security or compliance checks counts as `required_or_planned`. A pure risk or impact assessment requirement stays under CX-32b.
- `unclear`: The page makes an evaluative statement, but its subject, or whether it concerns this GenAI activity, cannot be settled. An evaluation clearly of a different tool or activity is `not_documented`, not `unclear`.
- `not_documented`: The page has no evaluation statement about this activity.
- CX-35..CX-39: no negative value; outcome claims need a described evaluation; risk/impact assessment counts only with testing or measured performance; vendor claims need a named institutional or independent evaluator; a pilot stage alone is `not_documented`.

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: narrow CX-32c to evaluation of AI systems
chosen.mechanism: Delete CX-32c's policy-review clause: a periodic review of the policy document is `not_documented` unless it requires testing, monitoring or evaluation of GenAI tools or their outputs.
chosen.benefits: Keeps 'evaluation' about system performance; reduces co-movement with policy_guidance.
chosen.risks: Reverses W3 = b and C3 = a (two signed rulings); policy-heavy institutions score lower.
chosen.commits_to: Re-signature of CX-32c; fixture pages (R-084); no enum change.

items.name: evaluation_type_* (CX-41, six yes/no, gated)
items.current_text: Included. Asked only when `evaluation_documented` ∈ {`results_reported`, `conducted_no_results`, `required_or_planned`}; six yes/no items: `pre_deployment_testing`, `pilot_evaluation`, `independent_audit`, `ongoing_monitoring`, `user_feedback`, `bias_or_safety_testing`.

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: gate on the post-downgrade value
chosen.mechanism: Procedural: ask (or keep) type items only if `evaluation_documented` is still positive after R-041 and R-081; otherwise store `_NA_`.
chosen.benefits: Prevents types without a supported evaluation; no wording change.
chosen.risks: Adds a dependency between T-024 and pass 2 (may need a third jev round, or post-hoc voiding).
chosen.commits_to: No re-signature if wording unchanged (procedural, PI approval); `_NA_` handling in T-012 enums.

items.name: content_* descriptive items (purpose, tool_or_model, vendor, data, users, status_date)
items.current_text: Items: `content_purpose` (what the tool is used for), `content_tool_or_model` (product or model named), `content_vendor` (supplier named), `content_data` (data inputs or data handled described), `content_users` (who uses it or who is affected), `content_status_date` (deployment status or date stated) ... each `yes` / `no` (yes = stated on the page).

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: keep page grain, gate by verdict
chosen.mechanism: Ask `content_*` only on pages with a GenAI-bearing verdict (the five R-003 values); store `_NA_` otherwise; reword to 'about any GenAI activity on the page'.
chosen.benefits: Avoids crediting background or no-GenAI pages; defines the referent.
chosen.risks: New wording, unpiloted; `_NA_` is a new value.
chosen.commits_to: Re-signature; enum change (two version steps); re-pilot.

items.name: content_contact (w4: named OR details)
items.current_text: `content_contact` = yes if either sub-item is yes (CX-01.2, contact wording w4): `content_contact_named` (a named person, office or unit given as responsible for the activity or for questions about it; a named official with no contact details counts, C1 = a) and `content_contact_details` (contact details anywhere on the page: email address, phone number, postal address or contact form, including press or vendor contacts and site footers).

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: retain footers in stored text
chosen.mechanism: Pipeline change: store a separate `chrome_text` (header/footer/nav) next to main text, and give jev both for the contact item only.
chosen.benefits: Makes the signed 'site footers' clause operational and markup-independent.
chosen.risks: Scraper change for one item; back-fill pages without stored chrome cannot be fixed without re-scrape.
chosen.commits_to: Scrape-layer change (new card, outside N-004's 'beyond follow-up links' boundary: needs PI ruling); no CX re-signature.

items.name: content_* safeguard items (human_oversight, risk_assessment, user_notification)
items.current_text: Safeguard items included, as Kaser does: `content_human_oversight`, `content_risk_assessment`, `content_user_notification`. **`content_user_notification` = yes only if the page describes a notice or label telling users they are interacting with GenAI or that content is AI-generated**; a page announcing that the institution uses GenAI is not by itself a notice (CX-01.1, W1 = a). The overlap with governance G1, G3, G4 is reported under R-070.

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: derive Group D has_* from the same question
chosen.mechanism: Ask each safeguard once per (page x activity) in pass 2 and derive both the page-level `content_*` (any activity yes) and the activity-level `has_*` (yes / not_documented) from it.
chosen.benefits: One question, no internal contradiction; cheaper.
chosen.risks: Changes the signed grain of CX-52 and the v2.5 vocabulary of `has_*` (which has `no` and `unclear`).
chosen.commits_to: Re-signature; Group D enum review (two version steps if values change); other reviewer's Group D items.

items.name: content_contact_emails (CX-53 deterministic @ extraction)
items.current_text: When `content_contact` = yes, extract the contact with a deterministic `@` search over the stored page text (e-mail regex in `pilot/contact.py`, `EMAIL_RE`) and store the list beside the code (`content_contact_emails`). No API call.

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: store internally, publish domain only
chosen.mechanism: Store the full list internally; publish only the domain part (and a count), or only role addresses (no personal-name pattern).
chosen.benefits: Keeps the PI's extraction; limits personal data in public/bulk outputs.
chosen.risks: Less useful to users wanting to contact the institution.
chosen.commits_to: Publication rule (PI ruling); D-007 interface; methods note. No change to CX-53 extraction text.

items.name: CX-60 'nothing found' normalisation (reported_outcomes / reported_incidents)
items.current_text: Deterministic step (no API): map all "nothing found" spellings to `none_reported`. The mapping table is published with the code.

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: jev decides existence first
chosen.mechanism: Pass-2 jev Choice on page text: does the page report an outcome (incident) of this activity: quantified / qualitative / none? The extractor extracts verbatim text only when not none; CX-60 then applies to legacy rows only.
chosen.benefits: Puts the classification with jev (R-001); CX-61 becomes the existence question itself.
chosen.risks: Changes CX-61's input from stored text to page text (see X10).
chosen.commits_to: Re-signature of CX-60/61; question-set change.

items.name: CX-61 outcome / incident kind (quantified / qualitative / none_reported)
items.current_text: Remaining text: a jev `Choice` over the stored text: `quantified` / `qualitative` / `none_reported`.

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: classify over page text with span
chosen.mechanism: Ask CX-61 in pass 2 over the page text with the activity span marked; the extractor then quotes support for the chosen value.
chosen.benefits: jev sees the evidence, not a selection; consistent with R-001.
chosen.risks: Larger state; wording change.
chosen.commits_to: Re-signature; question-set version bump; re-pilot.

items.name: CX coding grain and jev state (CX-01, CX-02, CX-05)
items.current_text:
- CX-01: **Page fields** (`disclosure_form`, `disclosure_scope`, the optional `content_*` items) are properties of the source page. They are coded once per (institution × page), on the stored page text, and copied to every evidence row from that page.
- CX-02: **Finding fields** (`evaluation_documented`, optional `evaluation_type_*`) are coded per (finding × page). The state given to jev is the page text plus that finding's `activity_name`, `activity_type`, `adoption_stage` and `tool_name`.
- CX-05: The raw jev answer is stored with its probability distribution, confidence, response model id and request id.

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: declare the state part of the frozen instrument
chosen.mechanism: Pin a `state_schema` per question set (fields, order, chunk marker) in the codebook; any change to it counts as a wording change.
chosen.benefits: Makes 'frozen' meaningful; programmatic linkage (RC-D-002 A) can hash it.
chosen.risks: Exposes that v2.7 already changes the state, so a re-signature is needed now.
chosen.commits_to: Re-signature of CX-01/02 with the v2.7 state; fixture re-run.

items.name: Supporting text per code (R-040)
items.current_text: For every jev code on a page or activity, the extractor (C-001) extracts the verbatim supporting text from the page, after jev has coded.

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: extractor quotes blind, before seeing the code
chosen.mechanism: Extractor is asked for the passages relevant to each field without being told jev's value; jev's code is then checked against them (X35).
chosen.benefits: Removes the confirmation incentive.
chosen.risks: More text per call; quotes may not match the specific value.
chosen.commits_to: SPEC delta to R-040 (PI approval); T-022/T-032 prompt approval.

items.name: Quote presence check (R-042)
items.current_text: Supporting text is checked against the stored page text by fuzzy match; a quote below the match threshold counts as no supporting text.

chosen.label: Keep R-042 with T-003 calibration
chosen.mechanism: rapidfuzz against stored text; threshold set by the PI after T-003.
chosen.benefits: As approved (Q-020 b, DEC-007 a).
chosen.risks: Short quotes pass trivially.
chosen.commits_to: T-003 spike and PI threshold approval.

items.name: Downgrade rule (R-041)
items.current_text: A positive or substantive code with no supporting text is downgraded: field to `unknown` (or the field's no-evidence value); institution verdict to `unclear` when no supported positive remains. Only positive or substantive values need support; `no`, `unknown`, `not_documented`, `_NA_` and negative page verdicts need none.

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: per-field target table
chosen.mechanism: Add a codebook column `downgrade_to` for every item (e.g. page verdict `confirms_activity` -> `ambiguous_genai`; yes/no items -> `unknown`, adding the value; genre -> `unknown`).
chosen.benefits: Makes R-041 executable and auditable; programmatic linkage can read the column.
chosen.risks: Adds `unknown` to yes/no items (enum change; CX items need re-signature).
chosen.commits_to: Codebook column; CX re-signature where values are added; two version steps.

items.name: Confidence threshold 0.8 for all jev codes (R-081)
items.current_text: One confidence threshold for all jev codes: 0.8. A code below 0.8 is downgraded as under R-041. This includes negative and absence codes: a page or field coded negative below 0.8 goes to `unclear` / `unknown`.

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: probability threshold by cardinality
chosen.mechanism: Threshold on the chosen value's probability (e.g. p >= 0.8 for every item), not jev's confidence.
chosen.benefits: Same meaning across binary and multi-value items.
chosen.risks: Different numbers from the ruled 0.8; needs re-sizing.
chosen.commits_to: SPEC delta to R-081 (PI ruling); T-024; quality packet re-sized.

items.name: Chunk combination rule (R-044, CX §11.1)
items.current_text: Chunked pages (> 32k tokens, C-004): the CX-01.2 §11.1 combination rule applies to every field. Page fields take the first chunk's value; yes/no items are yes if any chunk says yes; ordered vocabularies take the first value in table order found in any chunk. The supporting quote comes from the chunk that produced the code.

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: name the fields per rule
chosen.mechanism: Replace 'page fields' with an explicit list: first chunk = `disclosure_form`, `disclosure_scope`; any-yes = `content_*`, completeness 'incomplete', `evaluation_type_*`; ordered = `evaluation_documented`, page verdict (order to be ruled); state that combined confidence is the producing chunk's.
chosen.benefits: Unambiguous; matches §11.1; programmatic (codebook column `chunk_rule`).
chosen.risks: Needs a PI order over the 8 verdict values.
chosen.commits_to: SPEC delta to R-044 (PI); codebook column; A-021 fixtures updated.

items.name: Page completeness (R-030)
items.current_text: The first pass also records whether the page holds all available information about every activity it mentions, or links to further pages with information about any of them.

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: 'refers onward' question
chosen.mechanism: jev Choice: 'Does the page refer the reader to another page or document for more information about a GenAI activity it mentions?' yes / no; asked only on the five R-003 verdicts.
chosen.benefits: Answerable from text; fewer wasted fetches.
chosen.risks: Misses incompleteness the page does not signal.
chosen.commits_to: SPEC delta to R-030 (PI); T-011.

items.name: Follow-up links (R-031..R-036)
items.current_text: R-031: When a page is not complete, the LLM extracts the follow-up links and they are sent back to the scrape phase; fetched pages then pass through the same classification. R-032: ... up to 3 hops ... A per-institution cap on followed URLs also applies ... R-033: Any link the page cites is eligible, including news and vendor pages. R-034: Each URL is fetched at most once per institution per run; every followed link records the page it came from (provenance chain). R-036: Pages fetched live during the back-fill are new source records tagged with their provenance ... They count as evidence but sit outside the original searched sample and never add to its denominator.

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: tag discovery path on every source
chosen.mechanism: Add a deterministic `discovery_path` (searched / followed hop n / back-fill followed) on every source row in all runs, and report prevalence with and without followed pages.
chosen.benefits: Keeps comparability; no coding change.
chosen.risks: One more column.
chosen.commits_to: SPEC delta extending R-036 to all runs; D-007 field.

items.name: Supporting-text publication and length (R-043, DEC-016)
items.current_text: Supporting text is published with the code it supports. The API carries the full text; the website shows it up to a display cap, with a marker and access to the full text. (DEC-016 c: cap on website only, full text in API; cap value proposed by agent after T-003, PI sets.)

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: cap at extraction
chosen.mechanism: The extractor returns at most N characters (script-adjusted) per quote; the same cap applies in API and site.
chosen.benefits: Bounded payload and reuse exposure.
chosen.risks: Some codes need longer context.
chosen.commits_to: SPEC delta to R-043; T-022/T-032 prompts.

items.name: Contract version per row (R-050)
items.current_text: Every published row carries the contract version that produced it.

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: instrument manifest id
chosen.mechanism: Add `instrument_id` per row pointing to a manifest (contract versions, question-set version, jev model, extractor model + prompt hash, chunker, matcher + threshold, confidence threshold). See X36.
chosen.benefits: Full reproducibility; meets the PI's radical-transparency principle.
chosen.risks: One more table to maintain.
chosen.commits_to: SPEC addition; D-007; T-027/T-028.

items.name: source_type (Group E col 33, §4.6)
items.current_text:
| `official_gov` | Government domain (.gov, .gouv, .go, etc.), gazette, parliamentary record |
| `procurement_tender` | Tender notice, RFP, contract award, vendor selection document |
| `news_major` | Major national/international news outlet (Reuters, BBC, NYT, Le Monde, NHK, etc.) |
| `news_trade` | Technology or government trade press (GovTech, FedScoop, PublicTechnology, etc.) |
| `vendor` | Vendor website, case study, blog post, or press release |
| `academic` | Peer-reviewed paper, working paper, university report |
| `policy_org` | Think tank, IGO, or policy organization (OECD, World Bank, ITU, Brookings, etc.) |
| `social_media` | Official social media accounts (Twitter/X, LinkedIn from institutional accounts) |
| `archive` | Wayback Machine, Google Cache, or other archived page |
| `other` | None of the above; explain in `source_snippet` |

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: jev Choice in pass 1
chosen.mechanism: Add `source_type` to the pass-1 page question set with an order rule (first in table order) and the master official-site list in the state.

items.name: source_credibility hierarchy (col 35, §4.8)
items.current_text:
When sources conflict on coded values, the higher-credibility source wins:

1. **`high`**: Government domains, procurement/tender portals, parliamentary/council records, annual reports, regulator publications, gazette notices.
2. **`medium`**: Major news outlets, vendor case studies with named institutions, trade press, policy organization reports.
3. **`low`**: Social media, blog posts, undated pages, anonymous sources, machine-translated content you could not fully verify.

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: deterministic mapping
chosen.mechanism: `source_credibility` = fixed map from `source_type` (X21) plus `low` when `source_publication_date` = unknown; drop the translation clause.
chosen.benefits: Reproducible, free, consistent.
chosen.risks: Loses case-level judgement (e.g. an anonymous news blog on a major outlet's domain).
chosen.commits_to: Codebook mapping table; T-024 or T-028; Stage 6 tests.

items.name: Row-level confidence (col 38, §4.9)
items.current_text:
| `high` | Coded values are based on a primary government source or multiple corroborating secondary sources. |
| `medium` | Based on a single reputable secondary source without primary confirmation, OR primary source is ambiguous. |
| `low` | Based on indirect evidence, machine-translated sources with potential misinterpretation, or a single non-authoritative source. |

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: derive deterministically in Stage 6
chosen.mechanism: high = at least one supported `confirms_activity` source with credibility high, or two independent (non-syndicated, X38) sources; medium = one medium source; low otherwise.
chosen.benefits: Applies the criterion at the grain where it is answerable; reproducible.
chosen.risks: Mapping choices are substantive and need PI sign-off.
chosen.commits_to: Codebook rule; T-026; P-6 re-read.

items.name: uncertainty_flags vocabulary (col 39, §4.10)
items.current_text:
| `stage_ambiguous` | Cannot determine whether proposed, announced, pilot, or production |
| `genai_vs_traditional_ai` | Source mentions "AI" but unclear whether generative AI specifically |
| `institution_attribution` | Activity may belong to a parent ministry, sibling agency, or country-wide program rather than this specific institution |
| `date_uncertain` | Year of announcement or deployment could not be reliably determined |
| `source_language_barrier` | Key sources in a language you could not fully verify |
| `vendor_undisclosed` | Tool/vendor identity not publicly stated |
| `discontinued_uncertain` | Activity may have been discontinued but cannot confirm |
| `scope_unclear` | Cannot determine whether internal-only or also public-facing |

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: derive flags deterministically
chosen.mechanism: Compute each flag from codes (table above); add `identity_unresolved` for Stage 6 relations; drop `source_language_barrier`; `discontinued_uncertain` becomes a pass-2 jev yes/no.
chosen.benefits: No new judgement; consistent with the codes; removes the overload.
chosen.risks: Flags become a view of other columns (some may see them as redundant).
chosen.commits_to: Enum change (two version steps); T-024/T-026; data dictionary.

items.name: Stage 6 institution verdict (R-005; validate v1.3 §3.1; v1.4 complete-context rule)
items.current_text:
R-005: ... institution-level `no` only with complete supplied context and no unresolved signal. An institution whose reviewed pages are all negative at confidence ≥ 0.8 gets `no` directly; the complete-context rule blocks `no` only when an unresolved signal remains (a low-confidence negative downgraded under R-081 counts as one).

v1.3 §3.1: `yes` <=> `len(activities) >= 1` AND >=1 source has `genai_evidence = confirms_activity`. `no` <=> `len(activities) == 0` AND every source has `genai_evidence = confirms_absence`. `unclear` <=> `len(activities) == 0` AND no source has `genai_evidence = confirms_activity` (sources are some mix of `ambiguous` / `background_only`; at least one such source exists).

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: explicit truth table
chosen.mechanism: Codebook table: `yes` if >= 1 supported `confirms_activity` page with a supported activity; `no` if every attempted page (incl. failed fetches and unfollowed links) ends in {no_genai, confirms_absence, event_only, other_body} at confidence >= 0.8 and no page is ambiguous, background_only or failed; otherwise `unclear`. Variant for PI: allow background_only in `no`.
chosen.benefits: Reproducible, testable (A-010), no hidden choices.
chosen.risks: The background_only choice changes `no` rates materially either way.
chosen.commits_to: SPEC delta to R-005 (PI ruling on background_only and failures); T-026 tests.

items.name: Stage 6 activity identity and merging (R-005; v1.4 §9 relations)
items.current_text: R-005: explicit relations before merging observations; distinct/unresolved relations never merge. v1.4 §9: Allowed relations: same_activity, component_of_program, shared_participation, distinct_action, unresolved. ... Merged observations require a connected set of explicit same-identity relations. Distinct/unresolved relations cannot be silently collapsed; unresolved identities retain scope_unclear.

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: no merge without a jev relation
chosen.mechanism: Every pair of activity observations is asked, including identical names; candidate pairs pre-filtered deterministically only to skip obviously distinct pairs (different activity_type and tool), never to merge.
chosen.benefits: Identity is always a jev decision with evidence.
chosen.risks: More questions per institution.
chosen.commits_to: Codebook rule; T-026; cost estimate.

items.name: Stage 6 conflict resolution on Group D fields (v1.3/v1.4 §4.2)
items.current_text: After an evidence-based same-activity relation is established, compare independently supported Group D values using the source-credibility hierarchy from Output Contract §4.8 (Tier 1 = government / procurement / parliamentary; Tier 2 = major news / vendor case studies / trade press; Tier 3 = social / blogs / undated). Tie within a tier: most recent `source_publication_date`. Tie there: largest `source_snippet`.

chosen.label: Agent-drafted: jev answers the field over pooled evidence
chosen.mechanism: For a merged activity, jev answers each Group D question once over the union of the activity's supported quotes from all its sources (state = quotes with source type and date).
chosen.benefits: One coding rule for single and multi-source activities; no tie-break table.
chosen.risks: Pooled quotes can exceed state limits; new instrument.
chosen.commits_to: Codebook change; T-011 Stage 6 set; T-026; fixtures.
